title: IPMSM "Dモデル" モータ情報

source.citation: IEEJ Technical Committee on Rotating Machinery, public benchmark motor data, D model (from IEEJ Technical Report No. 1244, 2012)
source.licence: IEEJ terms of service: the CSV and DXF data may be used and redistributed with citation
source.note: The cache key is the DXF's SHA-256; the directory holds both pages, the DXF and the CSV files (manifest.json lists their SHA-256s), downloaded with the user's approval.

related.citation: H. Kaimori, K. Akatsu, Measurement and electromagnetic field analysis of IEEJ benchmark IPM motors, J. IEE Japan 135(2):75-82, 2015
related.use: Fig. 3(a): the phase of every slot of the authors' FE model.

machine.topology: inner rotor, one flat magnet per pole in a pocket with flux barriers to the surface, 24 slots with parallel-sided teeth, single-layer full-pitch distributed winding
machine.symmetry: One pole of four (90 degrees, as the DXF draws it) with antiperiodic radial ends and a sliding band in the gap; flux linkages and torque times 4. dq quantities from the phase flux linkages, with the d-axis on the rotor's north-pole axis and the phase-U axis and sequence from the winding's own MMF.

components_map.part: stator and rotor laminations, pocket, magnet, holes, slots
one-pole sector: antiperiodic ends, outer A = 0, sliding band in the gap

components_map.component: waveform_statistic assessor (fundamental and harmonic peaks, EMF from flux linkage, peak to peak)
dq_linkage assessor (stress torque, L_d and L_q against no load)

steel_bh.note: The JIS 50A350-equivalent curve the IEEJ committee publishes for the D model's core: single-sheet measurements to 2.05 T, extended above (the page describes the extension).

model_depth_mm.reason: The 2D analyses' depth is not stated; the stator stack length is the usual choice (the rotor's 67.5 mm overhang is a 3D effect).

stacking_factor.reason: Table 2 states 98% for the core; whether the 2D analyses applied it to the 50A350 curve (a single-sheet measurement) is not stated.

shaft_material.reason: The shaft material is not stated; the drawing's 8 mm-radius shaft is taken as non-magnetic.

hole_material.reason: The three holes of each rotor pole carry bolts in the real motor (the article says the rotor is clamped by bolts through its holes; the iron-loss table names iron and plastic bolts); the 2D analyses' choice is not stated, so they are air.

stator_contours.scale_reference: drawing units are metres: the bore arc is at 0.028 m and the rotor surface at 0.0275 m (Table 1's 55 mm rotor diameter)
stator_contours.note: Read with femm_brain.dxf (R12 POLYLINE, ARC and CIRCLE entities); coordinates times 1000. The drawing closes the slot opening centred at 67.5 degrees twice, by two bore arcs and by a chord no other opening has; the chord is left out (it would leave a 0.018 mm sliver).

rotor_contours.scale_reference: drawing units are metres: the rotor surface is at 0.0275 m (Table 1's 55 mm rotor diameter)
rotor_contours.note: As stator_contours; the drawing's radial segment across the gap at 90 degrees is left out (the sliding band draws the gap's ends).

slot_phases.figure: Kaimori & Akatsu (2015), Fig. 3(a), p. 76: the D model's FE mesh with each slot's phase label
slot_phases.scale_reference: slot labels counted counterclockwise from the slot centred at 7.5 degrees, the drawing's first slot (the DXF has slot centres at 7.5 + 15 k degrees)
slot_phases.note: Half the machine is drawn; the other two poles repeat the pattern. Single layer, full pitch (U+ and U- six slots apart).

contour_snap_mm.reason: Endpoint join distance; the drawing's coordinates repeat to 1e-14 mm.

fine_arc_deg.reason: Arcs at the rotor surface and bore in 0.12 mm pieces, about four element sides across the 0.5 mm gap.

min_arc_piece_mm.reason: No arc is cut into pieces shorter than this.

gap_air_mesh_mm.reason: Thin air regions of the gap.

pocket_air_mesh_mm.reason: Pocket and flux-barrier air, including the 0.055 mm clearances along the magnet.

conductors_per_slot.note: Single layer: each phase has slots/phases slots and each coil two sides, so series turns = conductors per slot x slots per phase / 2. With parallel paths the series model is the same, since each path's coils carry their share of the current.

flux_scale.note: The model holds one pole: each phase's two slots in it are a quarter of the phase's eight.

gaps.note: Not stated in text; Fig. 3(a) of the 2015 article labels every slot (slot_phases). The phase_linkage assessor checks the reading for balance and order.

gaps.item: whether 140 turns per phase are series turns
gaps.affects: every flux linkage and torque, in proportion
gaps.note: Turns per phase are series turns by the usual definition, and a series-circuit model is the same with any number of parallel paths. The other reading (140 counted over two paths) would halve every flux linkage; the measured magnet flux, a comparator, tests it. It cannot be a control: it needs 17.5 turns per slot, and FEMM takes whole turns.

gaps.affects: every flux linkage and torque, in proportion
gaps.note: The 60 mm stator length; control depth-rotor-length (67.5 mm).

gaps.item: whether the 98% stacking factor was applied

gaps.note: The stated remanence, 1.25 T, is used as given.
A magnetostatic 2D model gives neither losses from post-processing nor inverter waveforms.

findings: Nine of eleven acceptance targets pass (run2). The 2D magnet flux is 159.84 mWb against 160.6 (-0.47%), and the construction's phase linkage passes (balanced to 1.1e-4, phase order within 0.01 degrees). The 2D torque at 3 A rms passes from beta = 0 to 50 degrees, 0.04-0.82% from Table 4 (1.662 N m at 0 against 1.674; 1.853 at 25 against 1.852).

The torque fails at large current phase: beta = 60 gives 1.250 N m against 1.236 (+1.16%) and beta = 80 gives 0.458 against 0.450 (+1.74%). The model's d-axis inductance is 10.47 mH against Table 1's 10.70 (-2.1%) and its q-axis 26.17 against 26.30 (-0.5%). A larger Lq - Ld adds reluctance torque, which grows with beta, so this is consistent with the high-beta excess. The torque from the flux linkages agrees with the stress tensor within 0.03%.

Cogging is 0.253 N m peak to peak against Table 9's 0.072 (2D), 3.5 times. It is the same within 1% from the one-pole sector with a sliding band, the full cross-section with a sliding band (0.252), and the stress tensor on a meshed gap at 0.1 and 0.05 mm (0.251, 0.249; diagnostics outside the case). The cause is open. The page's sentence above Table 9 swaps the 2D and 3D values (0.079 and 0.072); the table is taken.

EMF harmonics (comparators): the 1st, 3rd and 5th are within 0.2%, 2.4% and 12% of Table 7's analysis column; the 7th is small in both (0.32 V against 0.16). Table 7's last row is labelled 9 but holds the 11th harmonic. Digitizing the paper's 2D EMF waveform (Fig. 17) gives orders 1-7 within 0.1-4% of the table, a 9th of 1.4 V and an 11th of 6.3 V. The model's 11th is 5.88 V against 6.44 (-8.8%).

Against the measured torques (comparators) the model is 3-9% high from beta = 0 to 50 degrees, +1.7% at 60 and -4.6% at 80, much as the paper's own 2D column is. The model's d-axis inductances are 15-19% below the measured ones (8.6% for a positive d current) and its q-axis ones 0.9-5.9% below; the measured values include the end winding, which a 2D model leaves out.

Controls: mesh 0.7 times moves every result by 0.1% at most. Solid steel instead of the 98% stacking factor moves torque by up to +0.44% and Lq by +1.5%. A steel shaft or steel bolts in the rotor holes each raise the flux by 1.5% and the torque by 1.1-1.9%. That would fail the flux target, so air, as assumed, agrees better. The 67.5 mm rotor length as the depth scales everything by +12.5% and fails the flux target, which supports the 60 mm stator length as the 2D depth.

run1 (kept) measured torque wrongly in two ways and passed only the flux. It multiplied the sliding-band torque by 4: the air-gap element's torque of an (anti)periodic sector is already the whole machine's. It averaged each current phase over six rotor positions 5 degrees apart, two of which fell in the ripple's dips, so the average read 2.7% low. Neither change touched an input, target or tolerance (commit 8fd5179). run1's phase_linkage failed only its check of the construction's predicted phase order, at a 1e-6 degree tolerance that drawing noise exceeds (5e-5 degrees); it now checks to 1e-3.
retrospective: Longest: the winding. The data page gives turns but not the layout. Fig. 3(a) of the 2015 article labels every slot, and the phase_linkage assessor confirmed the reading before any torque was compared.

The skill lacked rules for an air-gap element's torque scale on a sector, for averaging a rippled torque densely enough, and for checking a table's labels against the paper's own waveforms. All three are lessons now (51c5ba5), along with the power-invariant dq convention check that IEEJ's psi_m = sqrt(3/2) Psi1 needed.
Lessons that held: the authors' CAD drawing beats the table where they differ by 0.1 mm (stated in the geometry checks); inductances from single-axis currents are convention-free comparators.

Added generically: R12 POLYLINE support in the DXF reader (SPLINE and ELLIPSE refused), the harmonic_peak statistic with a time derivative and scale, power-invariant dq linkage, and L_d/L_q from single-axis currents.
